cat noun

also kitty, pussycat

classical

Traupman 141
Traupman 287

fēlēs, fēlis f.

noun, third declension

Other words

  • cattus, cattī m.

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Pallad. 4.9.4 (Morgan–Owens); Comen. OP 25: Fēlis (cattus) domum pūrgat ā mūribus; M-O s.v. cat; Andresian p. 25; Traupman 141; Traupman 287

    The late word behind the Romance and Germanic names; not in Lewis & Short. fēlēs is the classical word.

  • catta, cattae f. — cat, she-cat

    noun, first declension · also used · medieval · Joannes Diaconus, Vita Gregorii 2.60, ninth century (Morgan–Owens); M-O s.v. cat; Andresian p. 25; Traupman 141; Traupman 287

    In Martial (13.69) an unknown animal (Lewis & Short; Morgan–Owens prints 13.29); a cat from the ninth century.

See also meow.
